summary: Wasilla police are investigating allegations of kidnapping and sexual assault involving students from the hockey teams of two Fairbanks-area high schools, say they may charge five people, and the Fairbanks North Star Borough School District has suspended all hockey activity for both teams; everyone involved is a minor, nobody has been named and no charges have been filed. In court, calendar calls in two Fairbanks felony cases were continued and both trial weeks moved from Nov. 30 to Jan. 11, 2027, among them a kidnapping case; a fugitive from justice hearing was held and reset to Dec. 15. The Fairbanks court opened seven new criminal cases on Nov. 16 and 17, two of them on felony assault counts, one of which was dismissed the day it was filed. Fairbanks Police added three fraud reports to their Nov. 13 page, all at one block of the Johansen Expressway. The court filing counts below are the weekly report's own counts for Nov. 10 to Nov. 16 and so do not include the six cases opened on Nov. 17. A Delta Junction drunk-driving case was also called on Nov. 17 and continued to Jan. 19, 2027.

entries.title: Kidnapping and sexual assault investigation involving two Fairbanks-area high school hockey teams
body: Wasilla police are investigating allegations of kidnapping and sexual assault involving students from the hockey teams of two Fairbanks-area high schools. Amanda Graham, the Wasilla Police Department's public information officer, said police are looking at charging five individuals and that two Wasilla detectives recently traveled to Fairbanks to conduct interviews.

Graham said the alleged incidents occurred in Wasilla while the teams were in the Matanuska-Susitna valley for the Stars and Stripes hockey tournament, which Palmer High School hosted from Nov. 5 to Nov. 7.

The Fairbanks North Star Borough School District said it is investigating an incident involving students from the North Pole High School and Lathrop High School hockey teams, that it is coordinating with law enforcement, and that all hockey activities involving the two teams have been suspended as an interim safety measure. The district said the suspension is not a disciplinary determination and that it cannot release further details while the investigation is active.

Everyone involved is a minor and no names have been released. No charges have been filed. The alleged offenses are placed in Wasilla, outside the Fairbanks area, and would be prosecuted in the Third Judicial District rather than at the Fairbanks courthouse.

entries.title: Fugitive from justice hearing held: Brenden James Clarke
body: Brenden James Clarke is charged with arrest prior to requisition as a fugitive from justice, a charge that holds someone in Alaska while another state seeks his return. The offense is recorded at Fort Wainwright and dated Sept. 18.
A fugitive from justice hearing was held in Fairbanks on Nov. 17 and the court issued a further temporary order the same day. A new hearing is set for Dec. 15. Case 4FA-26-01857CR; Judge Seekins.

entries.title: Two felony trial weeks pushed to January: Dante Claxton and William Ostlund
body: Calendar calls in two Fairbanks felony cases were continued on Nov. 17 and the trial weeks in both, due to begin Nov. 30, were moved to Jan. 11, 2027. Both cases now have a calendar call on Dec. 22 before Judge Peterson.

Dante Nathaniel Larry Claxton is charged with kidnapping with injury or sexual assault, an unclassified felony punishable by up to 99 years, along with assault in the fourth degree and interfering with a report of a domestic violence crime, both Class A misdemeanors. All three counts are flagged as domestic violence related. The kidnapping count is recorded at North Pole and the misdemeanor counts at Fairbanks, all dated Sept. 22. Case 4FA-26-01890CR.

William Bruce Ostlund is charged with three counts of misconduct involving a controlled substance in the second degree, manufacturing or delivering methamphetamine, each a Class A felony punishable by up to 20 years. The counts are dated April 21, June 24 and July 8. Case 4FA-26-01818CR.
Both men are charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Drunk-driving case continued: Sara Mae Parlin
body: Sara Mae Parlin is charged with driving under the influence with a blood alcohol content of .08 percent or more, a Class A misdemeanor. The offense is dated Sept. 26 at Delta Junction.
A rural calendar call was held at the Delta Junction courthouse at 3 p.m. Nov. 17 and continued. Case 4DJ-26-00058CR; the next rural calendar call is Jan. 19, 2027, before Judge Young.

entries.title: Three fraud reports at one Johansen Expressway block
body: Fairbanks Police recorded three separate fraud reports at the 500 block of the Johansen Expressway on the morning of Nov. 13, all three taken by the same officer within six minutes of each other.

Each report covers a period that began weeks earlier: case 26003450 from Oct. 16, case 26003451 from Oct. 20 and case 26003452 from Oct. 31. No arrests have been made, nobody is named in the reports and no charges have been filed.

entries.title: Felony firearm assault charge filed and dismissed: Jerald Curtis Waters
body: Jerald Curtis Waters, 40, was arrested on a charge of assault in the third degree, recklessly placing someone in fear of serious injury with a dangerous instrument, a Class C felony punishable by up to five years. Police recorded an aggravated assault with a firearm at Cushman Street and First Avenue at 3:39 p.m. Nov. 16, and the arrest at First Avenue and Lacey Street at 3:40 p.m.; Fairbanks Police case 26003487.
The felony count was filed Nov. 17 in case 4FA-26-02301CR and dismissed by the prosecutor the same day. The case is closed and no charge stands.

entries.title: Felony assault and leaving the scene of an injury crash: Andre Lee Rue
body: Andre Lee Rue is charged with assault in the third degree, causing injury with a dangerous instrument, a Class C felony punishable by up to five years, along with driving under the influence, driving with a revoked license, driving in violation of license limits and leaving the scene of a crash involving injury.
The charges are dated Nov. 16 in Fairbanks. Case 4FA-26-02299CR; arraigned Nov. 17, preliminary hearings Nov. 25 and Dec. 7.

entries.title: Failure to stop for police: Christopher Allan Evans
body: Christopher Allan Evans, 40, of Fairbanks, is charged with failure to stop at the direction of a peace officer in the second degree, a Class A misdemeanor.

Troopers say their Criminal Suppression Unit tried to stop him on South Cushman Street Nov. 16 while he had two outstanding felony warrants, that he failed to yield and then ran on foot into the Lakeview Terrace trailer park, and that he was found hiding behind a trailer and arrested on the warrants.
Case 4FA-26-02300CR; arraigned Nov. 17, next court date Jan. 7, 2027.

entries.title: Missing person: Megan Baldwin
body: Troopers are asking for information about Megan Baldwin, 33, of North Pole, reported missing Nov. 16 after last being seen near Badger Road, Persinger Drive and Keeling Road. She was with a black pit bull mix, is about 5 feet 5 inches tall with dark hair, and her phone is disconnected.
Anyone with information should contact the Alaska State Troopers in Fairbanks.

entries.title: DUI arrest: James Sean Maska-Johnson
body: James Sean Maska-Johnson, 20, is charged with driving under the influence, a Class A misdemeanor. Fairbanks Police arrested him at Washington Drive and Airport Way at 2:21 a.m. Nov. 16. Case 4FA-26-02296CR.

entries.title: Driving in violation of an instruction permit: Sophia Christabeldell Simmonds
body: Sophia Christabeldell Simmonds, 18, is charged with driving in violation of an instruction permit, a misdemeanor. Fairbanks Police arrested her on the 1400 block of South Cushman Street at 11:30 p.m. Nov. 16. Case 4FA-26-02302CR; next court date Dec. 18.

entries.title: Criminal trespass charge filed: Timothy Royal Bidwell
body: Timothy Royal Bidwell is charged with criminal trespass in the second degree, unlawfully entering or staying on premises, a Class B misdemeanor, over his Nov. 15 arrest on South Cushman Street. Case 4FA-26-02297CR.

entries.title: DUI charge filed: Henry Cole Lilley
body: Henry Cole Lilley is charged with driving under the influence, a Class A misdemeanor, dated Nov. 17 in North Pole. Case 4FA-26-02298CR; arraignment Nov. 24.

entries.title: Driving with a revoked license: Hunter Marshall Freling
body: Hunter Marshall Freling is charged with driving with a license revoked after a prior conviction, a Class A misdemeanor, dated Nov. 12 in Fairbanks. The case was filed on a trooper citation. Case 4FA-26-02303CR.

entries.title: Injury collision on the Richardson Highway
body: A two-vehicle collision near Milepost 356 of the Richardson Highway at about 8:01 a.m. Nov. 17 sent a 61-year-old North Pole man to Fairbanks Memorial Hospital, troopers say. The other driver, 21, was cited for following too closely.

sources.label: Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, Nov. 17

entries.title: Court outcomes Nov. 10-13: two felony counts dismissed, Nenana DUI conviction
body: Prosecutors dismissed a third-degree sexual assault count, a Class C felony, and an assault count against Natalie Mestas on Nov. 10 (4FA-25-00635CR), and a third-degree assault count, a Class C felony, against Nicholas Edward Bell on Nov. 12 (4FA-26-02012CR).

At Nenana, Christopher Jaden Anthony Graham was convicted on guilty pleas of driving under the influence and possessing a weapon while intoxicated (4NE-25-00107CR); an assault count in a second case was dismissed under the plea agreement (4NE-25-00115CR).
Eighteen criminal cases in total were closed at the four Interior courts between Nov. 10 and Nov. 13, most by dismissal.
